963 rows that cannot appear on any timeline, cannot be graded weekly, and cannot age out.

input:
title: One Telegram bot token is shared by two Fly apps
body:
## The problem

`prospector-hermes` and `prospector-engine` hold the **same** `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` — identical
secret digest `5a07ce9efe76e6c8`. Telegram allows exactly one `getUpdates` consumer per token.

Today only `prospector-hermes` polls, so nothing is broken. The risk is that the second copy is
invisible until it fires: any release that enables a gateway or a poller in `prospector-engine`
reproduces #15 with no code change and no obvious cause.

## Why it is not just "unset it"

`prospector-engine` also holds `TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL`, which says it is meant to **send**. Sending
does not conflict — only `getUpdates` does. So the fix is not removing the token; it is making the
sender unable to poll.

## Remaining

- [ ] Find what in `prospector-engine` reads `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, and confirm it only sends
- [ ] Give the sender a token it cannot poll with, or gate polling behind an explicit env flag that
      is off by default (LAW 21: the default is closed)
- [ ] A guard that fails CI when two Fly apps share a `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` digest — the check is one
      `fly secrets list` per app and a digest comparison, so it is cheap
- [ ] Prove it: deploy, then `grep -c conflict` i

title: review-gate refuses 3 of 4 correct reviews: the match requires the literal word "session"
body:
The review gate refuses three of four natural ways to write a correct review,
because its match requires the literal English word "session".

`.github/workflows/review-gate.yml:171`

```
| map(select(test("session[^A-Za-z0-9]{0,12}" + $namere; "i")))
```

`$namere` is the escaped `Reviewed-by` name from the PR body. The comment must
therefore contain `REVIEW:` *and* the word "session" within 12 non-alphanumeric
characters of the name.

## Measured, five shapes, against the gate's own jq

```
PASS   REVIEW: KEEP — session chidionyema-a6
FAIL   REVIEW: KEEP — chidionyema-a6
FAIL   REVIEW: KEEP, reviewed by chidionyema-a6 this session
FAIL   REVIEW: KEEP — chidionyema-a6 (session)
```

Three correct reviews refused. LAW 38: a guard that refuses correct work is an
outage. Observed live on crew#179, run 32774362094:

```
FAIL: no issue comment or review contains 'REVIEW:' together with
'session chidionyema-a6' (e.g. 'REVIEW: <findings> — session chidionyema-a6').
```

The 12-character window is also arbitrary. "reviewed by chidionyema-a6 this
session" has the word and the name in the same sentence, in the natural order,
and fails on distance.

## The fix

Drop the literal word. Require

title: Spend guard: permit what the price list prices at zero, refuse what it does not
body:
Founder 2026-08-25 on CP3: "need to be seamless". rule-guard R14 refused the CP3 apply for an OCI Vault that Oracle's price list (apexapps.oracle.com/pls/apex/cetools/api/v1/products) prices at GBP 0: DEFAULT vault has no line item; key versions B92092 are 0 for the first 20 per tenancy; secrets have no line item.

**Founder, 2026-08-26: 'think bigger now.' Real pattern across tonight, not a one-off.**

Counted: OCI session-token auth (`estate-bootstrap`/`otto` profiles) expired and required a fresh founder browser login at least 5 separate times tonight, each time stopping live cluster verification cold (crew#286 CP2/CP3, crew#308, CP4/SPIFFE audit, this exchange). title: Apply crew#341's class-fix pattern (mature tool + adversarial fixtures + drill) across open P1s
body:
**Founder, 2026-08-26: "If we can apply this kind of pattern to our platform we will discover issues quicker? Add ticket so you don't forget to visit the class error tomorrow."**

## The pattern, concrete, from tonight (crew#341, idp PR#259)

Not a new idea -- LAW 45's own protocol, applied properly for the first time tonight end to end:
1. **Name the class**, not the instance ("no policy blocks secret-as-env-var", not "langfuse's chart does this once")
2. **Use the mature tool, verified against the real thing** -- fetched the actual upstream Kyverno community policy, ran it through the real `kyverno` CLI (not a hand-rolled simulator), found and fixed a real CEL compatibility bug in the process (documented, not hidden)
3. **Fixtures that prove both directions AND the false-positive risk** -- 2 must-fail, but 3 must-pass, including the deliberately adversarial edge cases (a guard requiring env to exist at all; ConfigMap vs Secret) that a naive guard would get wrong
4. **A permanent, re-runnable pytest incident test**, not a terminal command that gets forgotten
5. **A scheduled drill** (crew#341's `kyverno-secrets-drill.yml`, daily) so the gate proves itself over time, not just at PR

title: LAW: a founder directive rewrites every live session's goal by itself; no session reads a transcript and asks
body:
Founder, 2026-08-26 ~23:3xZ: "When a human types 'focus only on X' in any channel, an automated webhook immediately updates the goal-guard state file. The agent doesn't need to read the transcript and ask for permission; the physical goal state is already rewritten by the time the agent runs its next loop. If the agent hits a conflict, it is granted the authority to self-execute goal_graph.py --add '...' based on the most recent human directive."

Incident: a session froze on the idle-guard's 138 open items (crew#66 first) after the founder had already said "forget about fly, you have one mission", and reported BLOCKED instead of rewriting its own goal.

## What exists (LAW 39)
- `~/.claude/scripts/goal-guard.py`: per-session goal in `~/.claude/state/goal/<session>.json` (`write_state`), lane profiles in `~/.claude/lanes.json` re-read on every hook call.
- `~/.claude/scripts/goal_graph.py`: the task graph sessions claim from.
- estate-board hook (crew#102): every broadcast lands in each session's next turn; friction-relay carries standing rulings.
- Missing: nothing turns a founder line into a rewrite of every session's goal and the idle-guard's claim list.

input:
title: LAW: KINI checkpoints run as durable workflows on the estate's Temporal; 'Finish KINI' then close the laptop
body:
Founder, 2026-08-26 ~23:3xZ: "When the agent needs to run CP1 (Telegram to kernel), it doesn't run a bash script and wait. It dispatches a Temporal activity. Temporal handles the retries, the polling, and the state management. title: Six sessions, no written allocation: the lanes, and the two rules that stop the collisions
body:
Six interactive sessions are live right now and there is no written allocation, so
they collide. Measured on this machine in the last three hours, not remembered:

| repo | branch | commits in 3h |
|---|---|---|
| ~/.claude/scripts (claude-guards) | main | 53 |
| ~/.claude (claude-estate) | main | 14 |
| $REPO/crew | science/foundation | 10 |
| $REPO/hermes-v2 | deploy/fly-hermes-v2 | 5 |
| $REPO/maestro | fix/wal-and-circuit-breaker | 4 |

Fifty-three commits into one shared checkout is where the damage happens. Three
times today one session's `git add -A` swept another session's uncommitted files
into an unrelated commit on whatever branch happened to be checked out. Five files
written for the load-bearing sweep ended up on a test branch where nothing on main
could see them, and had to be recovered commit by commit.

## The two rules that stop it

**1. Never `git add -A` in a shared checkout.** Stage named paths. Every session
shares `~/.claude/scripts` and `~/.claude`, so `-A` picks up whatever another
session is holding. Name your files or use a worktree.

**2. One lane per session. Say which one you are in before you touch it.**
Claim it by replying on this issu

body:
Found while committing the LAW 39 inventory, 2026-08-24.

## What happened

`~/.estate/.gitignore` line 7 is `*` — deny everything, then re-admit by `!` line. A commit of
three files put two docs in and silently dropped `scripts/inventory.py`, and reported success:

```
git show --stat HEAD
 .gitignore                   |  1 +
 docs/demo/inventory.md       | 93 +
 docs/onboarding/inventory.md | 67 +
 3 files changed
```

The docs were describing an executable no repository held. Same shape as `~/.claude/.gitignore`
earlier the same day, which is what makes it a recurring issue rather than a bug — count is 2.

## Two blind spots in scripts/estate/in-git.py

1. **No `git check-ignore`.** `grep -nE 'check-ignore|ignored|gitignore' in-git.py` returns nothing.
   The sweep asks whether tracked files are committed. It never asks whether an untracked
   load-bearing file is untracked *because a rule refused it*, which is the silent case. An

The crew has no merge, deploy or cluster hand because those tools were never written — the control is that the code does not exist, and `tests/test_no_deploy_hands.py` greps for them. from crewai.hooks import on, InterceptionPoint, HookAborted

@on(InterceptionPoint.PRE_TOOL_CALL)

Memory(llm=..., storage=..., embedder=...,

body:
Parent: chidionyema/crew#850. Repo: `chidionyema/agent-workforce`.

## What exists today

`pyproject.toml` pins `crewai==1.9.3`. The current release is `1.15.20` — six minor versions of features the estate is paying for and not using. The crew also plans by prompt wording rather than with the framework's own planning, and there is no way to measure whether a change to the agents made the work better or worse.

## What to build

4. Wire `crew.test(n_iterations=..., eval_llm=...)` into a CI job that runs on demand, so a change to an agent's wording can be measured instead of argued about.
5. Set `max_execution_time` and `max_rpm` on the crew so one bad ticket cannot spend the day's budget.

The checkout today is: fill a form, it opens a pull request, a workflow flips the Flux switches, CI prices the result, and **merging the pull request is the switch**. A buyer reviews a diff in order to buy something. That is the friction that loses the sale.

ssh: $HOME/.colima/_lima/colima/ssh.sock [mux]

title: goal-guard.py:236 tmp->json rename race: 62 board rows in 24h, 38% of all board traffic
body:
Count: 62 guard-broken rows in 24h (of 164 total board rows), top-cost entry in LAWS.dynamic.md (cost 123). Fingerprint, verbatim: FileNotFoundError: '$HOME/.claude/state/goal/<session>.tmp' -> '<session>.json' at goal-guard.py:236.

Attribution (LAW 29): write_state() uses p.with_suffix(".tmp") — one tmp path per session id. Concurrent hook invocations in the same session both write that path; the first replace() wins, the second's tmp is gone. The decision at fault is the shared tmp name, not the rename.

Fix is one line: unique tmp per writer, e.g. p.with_suffix(f".{os.getpid()}.tmp"), replace() unchanged. Not applied because goal-guard.py is held dirty (+132 lines, goal-net tests) by another session — whoever owns that edit should fold this in. Same class as telegram_ledger.py PermissionError (37 rows/24h): guards failing while reporting, family #80/#81/#90.
